inconsistencies: #34533 and #36330 fix the same leak (wallet resubmission under -privatebroadcast) in opposite ways: route rebroadcasts privately vs. suppress resubmission entirely. #36607 is a broader guard covering the same class. Decide the approach on #36607/#36330 first; #34533 should not be merged independently.

#36374 and #36637 fix the identical Tor control password bug (backslashes in -torpassword). #36637 (hex-encoded token, explicitly allowed by control-spec) is the more robust approach and should be reviewed first; the other then closes.

Chain: #36437 is the base for #36506, and #36506 restates #36437's orphan-reassignment fix plus more. Review #36437 first, then #36506. #36486 fixes the same txid==wtxid forget hole that #36506's typed-forgetting commit addresses - coordinate so one is not merged blind to the other.

Chain: #36628 is the base reimplementation and #36608 extends it with package relay and the bitcoin-privbcast tool. Review #36628 first; a direction decision there determines whether #36608 is reviewed at all.

The private broadcast rework (#36628/#36608) removes or rewrites the subsystem that #34322, #36477, #36607, #36566, #34271 and #36670 modify. A direction call on the rework should precede detailed review of those six, or that review effort is wasted.
#36477 is a stated prerequisite for #36607 (P2) but is only P3 on its own merit; it must be reviewed before, not after, #36607.

#35600 (track in-flight manual connections) and #36014 (dedupe startup -addnode) address the same duplicate-manual-connection problem at different layers; #35600 is the general fix and should be reviewed first.
#36244 and #36445 both remove cs_main from the peer message loop; #36445 is close to a subset of the lock decoupling in #36244. Review #36445 first as the self-contained piece, or fold it in.

#35502 and #35522 are the same kind of move-only net_processing split and now share a band; both also collide with #34824 and #35561, which rewrite the same functions. Sequencing matters more than priority here.
#36716 supersedes the approach in #36688 (SO_OOBINLINE); only one should be pursued.
#35591 (Erlay) is explicitly DO NOT MERGE and will be carved into smaller PRs; its P2 band reflects the protocol's importance, not this artifact's mergeability.
result.notes: P1 is held to remote resource-exhaustion/memory-corruption vectors (#36521, #36015, #35888), the exploitable 1p1c relay-liveness holes (#36437/#36506), and the private broadcast reimplementation that removes a recurring deanonymization surface. The private broadcast cluster is the largest single sub-area here (ten PRs across all four bands) and its ordering is dominated by one unresolved direction question. Address-manager fixes, Tor/I2P connection fixes, net/net_processing restructuring, and test-only repairs were each grouped so a reviewer can take a cluster in one pass; within P3 I ordered behavioural fixes above structural work above tooling and tests, which moves several test-only PRs down relative to their individual scores.
